subject.title: CI: scope pull-request Node tests to affected targets

question: Should canonical pull-request Node CI replace the compact full-suite matrix with affected-target execution under the proposed fail-safe fallback policy?
rationale: This deliberately trades exhaustive per-PR Node coverage for queue capacity, so maintainers must confirm that the broad-fallback boundary provides the desired repository risk posture.

options.title: Adopt fail-safe targeting
options.body: Use the existing resolver on the merge-tree diff and fall back to the compact full suite for every broad, deleted, shared-harness, lockfile, unknown, or planner-error case.

options.title: Retain exhaustive PR coverage
options.body: Keep the compact full-suite matrix on every Node-relevant pull request and pursue capacity savings only through shard sizing, runner limits, or admission controls.

options.title: Stage an advisory rollout
options.body: Compute and report targeted plans alongside the full suite until comparison data proves that fallback classification preserves required coverage.

recommendation.title: Adopt fail-safe targeting
recommendation.body: Use the existing resolver on the merge-tree diff and fall back to the compact full suite for every broad, deleted, shared-harness, lockfile, unknown, or planner-error case.

likelyOwner.reason: The proposal owner also has the strongest recent history across the affected CI workflow and shard topology.
